newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now visiting Japan, has urged Japanese entrepreneurs to invest in labour-intensive industries in Bangladesh.

At least 40 people were injured and a cinema hall was set on fire during calshes between the acitivists of ruling Awami League and main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in southwestern Barisal district on Wednesday.
A domestic flight skidded off the runway while landing at Chittagong airport late on Wednesday, but there was no casulty.
Japan has agreed to lend support to carry out a technical study for the Ganges barrage.
Influx of Burmese muslim refugees into the southeastern districts has increased despite tight security along the border.
Ruling Awami League on Wednesday said that the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party was waging a "false and misleading" campaign against the 1997/98 budget.
With the Finance Minister retaining duty on textile machinery and development surcharge, private txtile mills owners hold a crucial meeting on Thursday to discuss the future of the sector.
The Advisory Committee on fertliser has asked the Energy Ministry to resume gas supply at the Chittagong Urea Fertiliser Factory. REUTER
